## [2026-10-28](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-28.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Concordat: Typed Sessions for LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.37461>)

This full-paper study evaluates an existing library that derives finite-state tool protocols from agent classes, exposes only currently legal tools and blocks illegal calls before execution. Its pressured airline experiments show why authorization should be checked separately from task success, while making the limits of keyword-based confirmation explicit.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:04:45.988+00:00 · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Tool Protocols, Authorization, Runtime Enforcement

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.37461v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/miladsikaroudi/concordat>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 3–5 and AppendicesA–C: the standard agent violates confirmation in 13/50 gpt-4.1 tasks and 29/128 Haiku task-runs, versus zero under the gate. Task success differs nonsignificantly. Newly-discovered catch-up: October 22 library and October 23–24 Haiku results precede the paper; October 26 repository history adds the gpt-4.1 study. Commit dates do not establish exact public visibility.

**Limitations:** The metric and gate share the same yes/yep/yeah test, so zero violations is conditional on that syntactic definition, not semantic consent. One simulated domain, quota losses, few trials and a between-model prompt revision limit generalization. Code was inspected, not executed.

### [Genie 4: A new generation of world simulation](<https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-a-new-generation-of-world-simulation/>)

DeepMind’s Genie 4 research preview combines real-time audiovisual world generation with Gemini-based scene grounding and a guiding agent that observes frames, plans steps, and checks their execution. This provides a concrete design for controllable simulated agent environments, while evidence for reliable training transfer or physical accuracy remains to be established.

**Published:** 2026-10-27 · **First seen:** 2026-10-28T10:07:19.756+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** World Models, Agent Environments, Interactive Simulation

[Blog](<https://deepmind.google/blog/genie-4-a-new-generation-of-world-simulation/>) · [Project](<https://deepmind.google/models/genie/>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The October 27 announcement’s “Simulating complex events” section describes Gemini 3.8 Flash as an observe–plan–verify loop around Genie; an Argon/robotics demonstration interleaves task-step captions with rendering. Native audio, interactive dialogue and natural-language scene edits are demonstrated. The full announcement and official model page were inspected; neither discloses training details, quantitative agent-learning evaluations, code or weights.

**Limitations:** Author-selected demonstrations and trusted-tester preview, not an independently evaluated simulator. Object permanence, spatial accuracy, complex physics, audio accuracy and long-session consistency remain limitations; no general simulation-fidelity or sim-to-real claim is supported.

## [2026-10-21](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-21.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Evolving Agent Interfaces](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601>)

Agent S4 evolves executable computer interfaces and usage knowledge from unlabeled synthetic-task trajectories, while a separate validation controller selects repositories and the task model and harness stay fixed. On 108 OSWorld V2 tasks, evolving a shared seed raises binary success from 19.44% to 21.30%, suggesting that reusable application interfaces can help a computer-use agent, although the reported aggregate includes 15 tasks used for repository selection.

**Published:** 2026-10-20 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.428Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Computer Use, Interface Evolution, Reusable Tools

**Public availability:** 2026-10-21T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28601>) · [Code](<https://github.com/simular-ai/agent-s>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Sections 2–7, Tables 1–4 and Appendices A/B plus mechanism prompts inspected. Population search alternates mutation/crossover for 30 descendants, with binary-tournament parent selection; the builder sees only 30 synthetic OSWorld training trajectories or 48 ScienceBoard synthetic trajectories and cannot access the 15 benchmark validation tasks/scores. Selection uses those validation scores, so the process is verifier-free only for construction evidence, not selection. Qwen3.8-27B and the Prime Agent harness remain fixed. Matched OSWorld results are 15.74% without a repository, 19.44% with the human seed and 21.30% with the best evolved no-scratch repository; full 108-task evaluation includes the 15 selection tasks. A separate ScienceBoard evolution reaches 58.58% versus 55.03% seed on 169 tasks, likewise including15 selection tasks. The 5.56% fixed-GUI comparison uses another harness/access surface and is not an isolated evolution gain. Original cs.AI October 21 batch and official schedule support inferred paper availability2026-10-21T00:00Z. The older Agent-S repository adds distinct S4 code in observed merge 58187e364e at October 21 at 05:32Z; no earlier S4-specific content release was established.

**Limitations:** Validation overlaps the final aggregate; final repositories have small single-run gains over a strong manually authored seed and no reported repeated full-benchmark confidence interval. The method changes available interfaces versus the fixed-GUI baseline, so the headline 3.8 times comparison cannot isolate evolution. Cost estimates assume 80% input-cache hits and exclude repository construction/infrastructure. Qualitative traces and successful-task token/call subsets do not establish uniform task latency savings. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-17](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-17.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Claude reveals ECDSA curve origins](<https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins>)

Anthropic documents an LLM-assisted investigation that tested pseudorandom-generator hypotheses and recovered the origins of several standardized elliptic-curve seeds and base points. Its published verification code makes this a useful case study of combining model-generated hypotheses with exact computational checks in scientific investigation.

**Published:** 2026-10-16 · **First seen:** 2026-10-17T10:06:03.000Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Scientific Discovery, Tool Use, Verification

[Blog](<https://www.anthropic.com/research/ecdsa-curve-origins>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The October 16 primary report explains generator scanning, hidden-state recovery, backward reconstruction and timestamp checks, and includes code and expected outputs for ten prime-curve seeds, four binary-curve seeds and six base points. Its stated sub-half-hour discovery is author-reported.

**Limitations:** A single investigation with an internal research model, not a controlled comparison or reusable agent-system evaluation. B-163 and several base-point origins remain unexplained; skipped candidate curves leave historical selection criteria uncertain. The result does not break ECDSA or demonstrate a weakness in the standardized curves. No independent reproduction.

## [2026-10-13](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13416>)

Web$hell compiles webpages into addressable information and action objects, letting agents search stored evidence and operate live controls through one interface. This makes complex web tasks easier to continue across many pages; the authors report stronger results on six search, navigation and research benchmarks with comparable or lower model cost than their tested interfaces.

**Published:** 2026-10-09 · **First seen:** 2026-10-15T04:39:34.000Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Web Interfaces, Persistent Evidence, Browser Actions

**Public availability:** 2026-10-12T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.13416>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Delayed discovery from the October 12 arXiv batch, absent the baseline and all 158 registry works; submission was October 9 at 11:23:40 UTC. Sections 3–6 and Appendices A–D expose deterministic compilation, persistent read-only prior states, controlled interface comparisons and association ablations. With GPT-5.6-Luna/high, Table 3 reports WebArena-Verified success 67.9% versus 57.8% for the combined search/browser/filesystem baseline.

**Limitations:** Work in progress using one principal model and finite benchmark subsets. Cost is model inference rather than total system cost: compilation adds 0.46–2.79 seconds per acquired page, and cached-token pricing affects comparisons. Stored page states cannot restore live browser state; no available implementation was verified and results were not independently reproduced.

## [2026-10-11](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-11.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Personal Agent Protocol: public draft 0.1](<https://sierra.ai/blog/introducing-personal-agent-protocol>)

Sierra published draft 0.1 of Personal Agent Protocol, specifying company discovery, delegated sign-in and sessions shared across web browsing, APIs and company-agent conversations. The draft gives builders a concrete integration contract for identifying agents and enforcing user-approved account scopes across channels. It remains a changeable draft with no reported performance or security benchmark, and its reference implementation is still planned.

**Published:** 2026-10-06 · **First seen:** 2026-10-11T10:05:27Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Agent Protocols, Delegated Authorization, Tool Integration

[Blog](<https://sierra.ai/blog/poppy>) · [Project](<https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The October 9 publication moves beyond the October 6 announcement to a public specification: sections 3-6 define discovery validation, OAuth flows, session/account tokens, browser-session assertions and API authorization. This is a delayed discovery of a concrete interoperability design, not an experimentally validated reliability result. First-seen uses the canonical-source review checkpoint; the earlier search encounter was not precisely logged.

**Limitations:** Draft 0.1 permits incompatible changes. Broad read/write scopes require company enforcement; mediated sign-in handles credentials, MCP uses resource-specific bearer tokens, and revocation of already issued session tokens depends on enforcement. No controlled benchmark or independent security evaluation is supplied. The promised reference implementation was not verified as released.

**Update:** 2026-10-09: https://sierra.ai/blog/poppy releases the public draft at https://personalagentprotocol.org/docs/spec, whose header confirms the update date. The October 6 announcement only promised a later specification; the new contribution is an inspectable protocol contract. The original October 6 publication date and canonical identity are preserved; no new standard adoption or demonstrated security guarantee is inferred.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793>)

SWE-agent builds a model-oriented interface for repository search, file editing, and test execution, with concise feedback and checks that help agents recover from mistakes. It establishes interface design as a practical source of coding-agent improvements and supplies an open implementation for studying tool ergonomics.

**Published:** 2024-05-06 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Coding, Tool Use, Agent-Computer Interface

**Positioning:** open-reference

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2405.15793>) · [Code](<https://github.com/SWE-agent/SWE-agent>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The paper's Table 3 isolates editing, search, file-viewing and context choices; its GPT-4 Turbo setting resolves 18.0% of SWE-bench Lite versus 11.0% for a shell-only agent. The arXiv history records v1 on May 6, 2024 and v3 on November 11, 2024; the code repository is accessible.

**Limitations:** Historical results use older models, task sets and per-instance budgets and should not be interpreted as a current coding leaderboard. Better interfaces reduce specific errors but do not ensure successful repair.
